problem: Offer a legal, simple way to buy music for the iPod.
title: Apple launches the iTunes Music Store with 99-cent songs and no subscription
context: Online music was dominated by file sharing and subscription services.
decision_made: Sell songs individually at 99 cents each with no subscription fee, from major labels.
action_taken: Launched on 28 April 2003 with about 200,000 songs.
observed_outcome: Apple reported over one million songs sold in the first week against an internal goal of one million in the first month; TIME later summarised more than 50 million songs in the first year.
lessons: Simple pricing and legal convenience can beat piracy and subscriptions when paired with a device ecosystem.
limitations: First-week figure is from Apple's own press release. Apple also sold the iPod, so the store's profit contribution was not measured here.

claims.claim_text: Apple launched the iTunes Music Store with songs at 99 cents and no subscription fees.
Apple said the store sold over one million songs in its first week.
